newsitem.title: INDIA: India cotton pulled up by limited supplies, hike.
newsitem.headline: India cotton pulled up by limited supplies, hike.

text.p: Cotton prices climbed on the local market on Tuesday as limited supplies and a price hike by state-owned agencies dragged the market upward despite low mill buying, dealers said.
Supplies were low due to widespread rain in producing centres.
In spot deals Bengal-deshi jumped up to 1,050/1,110 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) from 1,000/1,075 rupees while Punjab saw-ginned rose by 20/30 rupees at 1,850/1,875 rupees per maund.

"The state-owned Maharashtra Cotton Grower's Federation has hiked selling prices of cotton by 100 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) upto August 14 and thereafter price hike will be 200 rupees per candy," one broker said.

In the Gujarat segment Kalyan cotton rose by 300 rupees at 14,500/14,700 rupees per candy while Wagad cotton rose by 100 rupees at 13,100/13,200 rupees and Kala-ginned rose by 100 rupees at 12,400/12,500 rupees per candy.
